audit_findings.title: Redeemable NCI put is an unmodeled claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.022 billion filed redemption value at June 30, 2026, equal to $16.91 per diluted share and 6.1% of the $81.719 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The put creates a claim in the equity bridge, while exercise would add the minority Indices owner earnings and potentially financing costs to OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Specifically, this amount relates to the put option under the terms of the operating agreement of S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC, whereby, after December 31, 2017, CME Group and CME Group Index Services LLC (“CGIS”) has the right at any time to sell, and we are obligated to buy, at least 20% of their share in S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted contractual obligation is demonstrated and large enough to affect the valuation materially. However, deducting the entire redemption value without adding the acquired 27% earnings would also be inconsistent, so the net value error and direction cannot be established from the current record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the post-spin put agreement, current redemption calculation, exercisable percentage and expected timing; rerun the valuation with the redemption payment, incremental minority owner earnings, taxes and funding costs modeled together.

audit_findings.title: Mobility was removed using a profit share that is incompatible with owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the current haircut removes $300.6 million, while filed Mobility D&A less capex alone was $292 million and its segment operating profit was $378 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The proportional haircut directly affects anchor OE and therefore every explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: 2025 and 2024 include amortization of intangibles from acquisitions of $303 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The measurement mismatch is demonstrated: Mobility's 5.73% share of operating profit reflects $303 million of acquisition amortization that the OE calculation adds back. The available figures strongly indicate that $300.6 million understates the cash earnings removed, but taxes, working capital, corporate allocations and post-spin interest prevent a reliable correction amount.
audit_findings.action: Construct Mobility-attributable OE from after-tax operating earnings, its filed $320 million D&A and $28 million capex, working-capital investment, stranded corporate costs and debt-related interest changes; then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Parent-attributable earnings are mixed with consolidated cash-flow add-backs
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $9.9 million of current anchor OE after the 5.73% haircut, computed from 27% × ($43 million Indices D&A − $4 million capex) × 94.27%; approximately $156 million or $0.52 per share in the base valuation
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated Indices D&A and capex add-backs increase OE even though the starting income already excludes earnings attributable to the 27% minority owner.
audit_findings.evidence: The entire amount of this revenue is included in our consolidated statement of income and the portion related to the 27 % noncontrolling interest is removed in net income attributable to noncontrolling interests.
audit_findings.explanation: The basis mismatch is demonstrated, but the filed segment figures limit it to about 0.2% of the $4.945 billion anchor and about 0.2% of base equity value. Correcting it would not approach the gap between the $275.24 base value, $321.99 bull value and the $450.58 market price.
audit_findings.action: Allocate Indices D&A and capex 73% to SPGI in the next rerun and verify whether any other consolidated cash-flow adjustments contain a minority-owned portion.

audit_findings.title: Finite acquisition-amortization tax shields may be capitalized into perpetuity
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed 2025 book amortization was $1.069 billion, and definite-lived intangibles are amortized over periods of up to 25 years
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back book amortization can leave a current tax shield in OE that is then grown and included in terminal value after the underlying tax deductions expire.
audit_findings.evidence: Definite-lived intangible assets are being amortized on a straight-line basis over periods of up to 25 years.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved modeling possibility, not a demonstrated error. The valuation's terminal value represents 47.7% to 52.6% of operating value, so a tax shield improperly continued into perpetuity could matter, but the filings do not provide tax-basis amortization schedules or establish that book and tax amortization coincide.
audit_findings.action: Obtain tax-basis amortization and deferred-tax reversal schedules by acquisition, forecast the surviving cash tax shields through year 10, and rerun terminal OE without expired shields unless replacement acquisitions and their funding are explicitly modeled.

audit_findings.title: Disposed OSTTRA earnings may remain in the recurring anchor while sale cash is also added
audit_findings.magnitude: at most $28 million of annual pre-haircut earnings; $26.4 million after the 5.73% haircut, implying approximately $414 million or $1.40 per share in the base valuation if fully capitalized
audit_findings.mechanism: Unremoved OSTTRA equity income would inflate anchor OE and terminal cash flows while the post-sale cash remains in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: On October 10, 2025, the Company and CME Group completed the sale of OSTTRA to Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co. (“KKR”), a leading global investment firm.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the $28 million was normalized out is unresolved. Even assuming none was removed, the amount is about 0.53% of whole-company OE and about 0.5% of base equity value, far too small to alter the conclusion that market price exceeds even the bull value.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $28 million OSTTRA equity income through the 2025 OE normalization and remove any residual recurring amount; confirm that the $270 million disposition gain was separately excluded and that sale proceeds are included only through post-event cash.

audit_findings.title: Growing capitalized sales commissions may be omitted from reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $58 million filed increase during 2025, equal to 1.17% of the $4.945 billion anchor and approximately $910 million or $3.07 per share in the base valuation if treated entirely as recurring omitted reinvestment
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash additions to capitalized contract costs are not conventional capex; failing to deduct additions net of the amortization already charged in net income can overstate OE and understate reinvestment needed for growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Total capitalized costs to obtain a contract were $ 349 million and $ 291 million as of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, respectively, and are included in prepaid and other current assets and other non-current assets on our consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is possible but not demonstrated because the balance change does not separately identify cash additions, amortization, acquisitions, dispositions or currency effects. Even treating the entire $58 million increase as recurring omitted reinvestment changes base value by only about 1.1% and does not affect the valuation conclusion; the balance also declined from $349 million to $338 million during the first half of 2026.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile contract-cost cash additions, amortization, acquisition and currency effects for 2025 and post-spin continuing operations; deduct recurring net cash investment in the OE rerun without double-counting commission amortization.
